prerequisites: Basics of technical physics (thermodynamic diagrams, first and second law of thermodynamics, gas laws, equation of fluid motion)
Basics of chemistry (balance of elementary chemical reactions)

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire basic knowledge about volumetric pumps and positive displacement compressors.
Acquire basic knowledge about cooling systems.
Acquire basic knowledge about heat pumps.
Acquire basic knowledge about internal combustion engines.

syllabus_topics: Volumetric pumps: architecture, ideal and real indicator diagram, characteristic curve, total efficiency (volumetric and hydromechanical efficiency), flow rate regularization with double-acting pump and pneumatic compensator, multiple plunger pumps, types (external and internal gear, vane, diaphragm, peristaltic, screw pumps).

Centrifugal pumps: flow in rotor channel, Euler equation, architecture, suction and delivery speed triangles, theoretical prevalence, fluidodynamic losses, actual head, prevalence at zero flow, link between prevalence and pressure increase.
Efficiency of a centrifugal pump: total, hydraulic and mechanical efficiency, torque and power trends.
Hydraulic similitude concept for characteristic curve at different rotation speed.
Priming a centrifugal pump, suction pressure calculation.
Cavitation phenomenon, NPSH definition (pump and plant), NSH diagram usage.
Elementary design of a centrifugal pump.
Transition from centrifugal to axial pump, axial blades (speed triangles near hub and blade end).
Multicellular centrifugal pump for high prevalence values, balancing axial thrusts.
Determination of the operating point of a pump in a hydraulic circuit.
Characteristic curve of pumps arranged in series and in parallel.
Hydraulic resistance of branches arranged in series and in parallel.
Operating point of a centrifugal pump in a non-elementary hydraulic circuit.
Test circuit of a pump: main elements (tank, flow measurement, pressure difference measurement, valve, heat exchanger, pressure limiting valve).
Operational differences between centrifugal and volumetric pumps.
Comparison between characteristics of centrifugal and volumetric pumps based on flow rate and prevalence.
Operational fields of centrifugal pumps, multicellular pumps, and axial pumps.
Volumetric compressors: architecture of alternative volumetric compressor, ideal and real indicator diagram, dead volume, volumetric efficiency, compression ratio limit, stage work and specific work.
Optimum stage compression ratio in two-stage compressor, extrapolation to n stages.
Architectures of volumetric compressors: single-acting, double-acting and multi-phase reciprocating, vane, liquid ring, screw, and Roots.
Internal combustion engines: introduction, architecture, main definitions.
Theoretical thermodynamic cycles: Otto, Diesel, Sabathè (transformations and efficiency).
From ideal indicator diagrams to real ones, mean temperature of exhaust gases.
Engine power via thermal analysis, lower heating value, indicated and effective mean pressure, simplified expressions of engine power and torque.
Efficiencies: combustion, thermodynamic, indicator, volumetric, mechanical, total and thermal efficiency, link between thermal efficiency and specific engine consumption.
Relationship between main geometrical engine parameters: mean piston speed, stroke/diameter ratio.
Engine performance curves (torque, power and specific consumption).
Relationship between single and multi-cylinder engines with same power/displacement, cylinder number limit, multi-cylinder engine architectures.
Engine load control: quantity of mixture (spark-ignition) and quality of mixture (compression-ignition), effects evaluation.
Combustion process in gasoline and Diesel engines, influence on architecture.
Concepts: combustion speed, flame front, equivalence ratio, auto-ignition delay, stoichiometric air-fuel ratio, knock.
Fuel injection systems: gasoline engines (electronic control, speed-density system, port injection, direct injection), Diesel engines (common rail).
Polluting emissions: formation, control, post-treatment.
Auxiliary systems: lubrication circuit and power absorption limitation.
Supercharging: centrifugal and volumetric compressors, intercooler contribution.
2-stroke engines: architecture, indicator and performance diagrams.
teaching_methods: Use of tablet connected to projector for concept development and material display
assessment_rules: The assessment consists of an oral exam lasting about 45 minutes, where the student answers two randomly selected questions from a list. The evaluation is expressed in thirtieths, based on the student's autonomy, exhaustiveness, and precision in explaining arguments and sketching. For the integrated course, the final grade is the arithmetic average of the grades obtained in the two modules, rounded up if the decimal is 0.5. To achieve "30 cum laude", the student must receive "30 cum laude" in both modules or "30 cum laude" in one and "30" in the other.
